faq: Which platforms can you plan a move between?

Most common ones, including Shopify, WooCommerce, BigCommerce, Wix, Squarespace, Magento and PrestaShop. If yours is less common, tell us in the order form and we confirm before you pay whether we can review it.
Do you need to log in to my current store?
We ask for staff access with limited permissions, never your password. Read-only access is enough for the plan. If you prefer, you can send exports of products and orders instead.
Do I have to hire you to do the move afterwards?
No. The plan stands on its own and any developer can follow it. If you want us to carry it out, we quote each part at a fixed price using the plan as the scope.
What if my new platform is not decided yet?
Then order Platform Advice first, or pick Standard and we outline the plan for your two top choices. A move is much cheaper once the target platform and its limits are known.

desc:
Ecommerce store migration planning is the written plan you make before moving a store to a new platform. Ecom Swift LLC reviews your current store and delivers a checklist, a timeline and a clear list of what moves, what is replaced and what stays behind.

## What is ecommerce store migration planning?

Migration planning is the stage before any data is copied. It answers practical questions. What is in the store today? Which parts must move, which can be rebuilt and which are no longer needed? In what order should the work happen, and how will you know it is finished?

The result is a document you can follow, share with a developer or hand to your team.

## Why planning prevents most migration problems

Most failed moves share one cause: nobody knew what was inside the old store. Hidden apps, old landing pages, custom code in the theme and special shipping rules only appear once something stops working. Fixing those after launch costs more than finding them at the start.

A plan also stops the project from growing quietly. When the list of tasks is written down, a new idea has to be weighed against the timeline instead of being added on the day before launch.

## How a plan protects sales and search traffic

Your store earns money every day, so the move should interrupt that as little as possible. A plan chooses a launch day that fits your calendar, such as a quiet weekend, and sets a freeze on old-store changes so no orders or edits are lost.

It also protects search traffic. Product and collection addresses change when you switch platforms. If redirect work is listed early, it gets done. If it is forgotten, pages that used to bring visitors from Google return error pages.

## What a good migration plan contains

- An inventory of product types, collections, pages, blog posts and policies.
- Counts of products, customers and orders that will be moved.
- A list of apps, scripts and integrations, with a decision for each.
- A note on special features such as subscriptions, bundles or custom fields.
- Field mapping between old and new platform, down to the column.
- An order of steps, so nothing depends on something not yet built.
- A timeline with a suggested launch day and a freeze window.
- Test cases that prove the new store works before the switch.
- A rollback route if launch goes wrong.
- A short plan for telling customers about the change.

## What we do

We study your current store from the outside and, where you grant access, from the inside. We count what is there, list what is attached to it and note the risks. Then we sort every item into three groups: move as it is, rebuild or replace, and leave behind.

From that we write the plan. The Basic package gives a short review and a one page checklist. Standard adds counts, an app inventory, a timeline and a planning call. Premium goes further with field-by-field mapping, test cases, a rollback plan and a review call after you have made changes.

You are free to use the plan with us, with another team or on your own.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Decide your reasons for moving before the plan is written.
- Share the apps and features you rely on every week.
- Set the launch day around your slowest sales period.
- Agree who approves each step.
- Keep the plan as a living document until launch.

**Avoid:**
- Starting the data export before the plan exists.
- Assuming all features exist on the new platform.
- Forgetting the pages that only your old customers know.
- Moving during a major sale or holiday rush.
- Letting several people change the old store during the move.

## Who this is for

A store owner who knows a move is coming but does not know where to start. A business that has been quoted for a migration and wants a second view of what is needed. A team preparing a large catalog who need a shared checklist.

## How to get started

Send us the address of your current store and the platform you are considering. Tell us what worries you most, such as search traffic, customers or downtime.

If you want us to look inside, give us staff or collaborator access to the old store. Passwords are never required, and read-only access is enough for planning.
